title: Wild Boar in Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: Meeting them, dogs, gardens, feeding and who to call.

items.q: What should I do if I meet a wild boar in Berlin?
items.a: Stay calm, stand still or walk back slowly, and keep a good distance. **Always leave the animal a way out.** Never corner it, and turn back from a sow with young.

items.q: Are wild boar in Berlin dangerous?
items.a: Usually not. City boar are used to people and rarely attack. The risk rises when a boar is **cornered**, when you come between a **sow and her piglets**, or when a **dog** chases it.

items.q: Is it illegal to feed wild boar in Berlin?
items.a: Yes. Feeding wild animals is banned under Berlin's state hunting law, and the fine can reach **5,000 euros**.

items.q: How do I keep wild boar out of my garden?
items.a: A solid fence about **1.50 m high**, dug about **40 cm** into the ground and bent outwards at the bottom. Keep compost inside it, keep bins closed and never dump garden waste at the forest edge.

items.q: Who do I call about a wild boar in Berlin?
items.a: Call **110** if people are in danger, a boar is inside a building or you hit one with a car. For advice, call the **NABU wildlife line on 030 54712891** during its office hours. Report a dead boar to the forestry office or the district office.

items.q: When are wild boar most active in Berlin?
items.a: Mostly at **dusk and at night**, especially where people disturb them by day. The mating peak is **November to January**, and most piglets are born in spring.

items.q: What should I do if I hit a wild boar with my car?
items.a: Secure the scene, call the police, and pull the animal to the roadside only if it is safe. **Never put it in your car.** If it ran off injured, mark the spot and do not follow it.
